full_judgment: 3. The defendant No. 1 contested the suit contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable in its present form the plaintiff's story of acquiring of title on the basis, of said pattas and the Kabalas are denied by the defendant No. 1. He further contended that the said three documents were not benami transactions and neither Sudhendu Nath Roy nor Sarala Sundari was the benamider of the plaintiff. No consideration did pass at the instance of the plaintiff herself with regard to the said three documents. It was further contended by the Defendant that the plaintiff was never in possession of the suit properties and she acquired no title in the same as benamder of Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari. The defendant further contended that Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari acquired the suit properties in their own names with their own modify and the RS records were correctly prepared in their names. While thus in possession on the owners i.e. Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari settled the suit property with the defendants on 28th Chaitra 1360 BS at a jama of Rs. 15 and delivered possession to him. The defendant No. 1 is in possession of the suit land since the settlement in his favour. As SA Khatian did not record the name of the defendant in spite of his settlement he brought Title Suit No. 449 of 1961 before the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, Barisal against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari and obtained a decree after due service of summons upon the said two persons. The said decree was bonafide and could not be called into question by the plaintiff. As Sudhendu Nath Roy and Sarala Sundari leased out the suit property to the defendant No. 1, the husband of the plaintiff subsequently obtained the original pattas and kabala clandestinely and brought Title Suit No; 267 of 1960 and obtained a fraudulent decree against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari in respect of the suit property. Neither the plaintiff nor her husband ever posseted the suit property or realised any rent from tenants. The defendant further contended that the decree obtained by the defendant against Sudhendu Nath and Sarala Sundari was bonafide and valid decree after due service of summons upon them at their Barisal residence. The husband of the plaintiff is the proprietor of the Sonali Cinema Hall. His business is to acquire properties of thereon resident Hindus and to prepare false and forged documents in his name from the aforesaid non-resident Hindus. It was further staged that the suit of the Plaintiff is hit by Ordinances I and VI of 1964 and the Plaintiff has no locus standi or any legal character to file the present suit.
